metrics.description: The proportion of true Trojan nodes (trigger DFFs and payload gate) correctly identified in the report.
metrics.name: detection_rate

metrics.description: The proportion of reported suspect nodes that are not part of the actual Trojan.
metrics.name: false_positive_rate

metrics.description: The wall-clock time taken by the evaluation script to grade the submission, measured in seconds.

acceptance_criteria: All trigger DFFs (SR1) are correctly identified and labeled.
The payload XOR gate (SR2) is correctly identified and labeled.
No more than 2 false positives (incorrectly reported nodes) are present in the submission.
hidden_spec.ground_truth: The labeled trigger DFFs recognize input sequence 1101 across four cycles; the terminal state enables an XOR on data_out[2].

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Simulate the netlist exhaustively for short sequences and compare the reported trigger nodes against the hidden ground truth list of DFF instances. A node is correctly identified if its hierarchical name matches exactly.
security_requirements.requirement: The submitted report must correctly identify all D-type flip-flop instances that form the 4-state sequence recognizer for the '1101' pattern.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Trace the fan-in of the data_out[2] output port. The report must list the exact instance name of the XOR gate that has the Trojan's enable signal as one of its inputs.
security_requirements.requirement: The submitted report must correctly identify the specific combinational gate that performs the XOR corruption on the data_out[2] signal.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: For each correctly identified node, verify that the associated 'role' string in the report matches the expected role from the ground truth.
security_requirements.requirement: The submitted report must correctly label the identified nodes with the roles 'state_register', 'trigger_logic', or 'payload_gate'.

hidden_spec.threat_model: An attacker has inserted a Hardware Trojan into the gate-level netlist. The Trojan's trigger is a four-state sequence recognizer implemented with DFF primitives that activates upon observing the input sequence 1101 across four clock cycles. The payload is an XOR gate that corrupts the data_out[2] signal when the trigger's terminal state is reached. The activation logic is distributed across several flip-flops to evade simple combinational rare-net analysis.

constraints: The netlist is a flat, synthesized gate-level Verilog file.
The design contains a finite state machine implemented with standard cells and D-type flip-flops.
The analysis must be performed on the provided netlist without modification.
expected_outputs: A valid trojan_report.json file in the submission directory.
The report must contain a list of suspect nodes with associated labels.
The report must be parseable JSON conforming to the specified schema.

functional_requirements.requirement: The submitted trojan_report.json file must be syntactically valid JSON and parseable by a standard JSON parser.
The report must contain the top-level key "suspect_nodes" with a value that is an array.
Each element in the "suspect_nodes" array must be an object containing exactly two keys, "node_name" and "role", both with string values.

public_spec.interface: The participant must produce a single file named trojan_report.json inside the submission/ directory. The file must be valid JSON with the following structure: an object containing a key "suspect_nodes" which maps to an array of objects. Each object in the array must have two string fields: "node_name" (the exact hierarchical name of a net or cell instance from the netlist) and "role" (a short label describing its suspected function, e.g., "trigger_logic", "payload_gate", "state_register").
public_spec.objective: Analyze the provided gate-level netlist and identify any suspicious sequential logic structures and their downstream effects. Submit a report listing all suspect nodes and their roles.
public_spec.response_format: A JSON file named trojan_report.json with the following schema: {"suspect_nodes": [{"node_name": "string", "role": "string"}]}

title: Sequential trigger Trojan in a gate-level controller
